title: I almost took steroids (Story Time)
summary: NH tells how, around 2016-17 and six years into lifting, a dirty bulk, bad programming and YouTube fitness left him plateaued and blackpilled enough to plan to start PEDs. Spending time with a group of enhanced lifters at his US university gym, who trained poorly, lost their gains when they came off and in three cases died, convinced him to stay natural for life.
claims: Nearly every lifter will at some point feel the urge to take PEDs; it is tempting and close to inevitable
He moved from France to the US in 2015; before that all his training was at home in his bedroom with dumbbells and bodyweight
Joining a real gym and watching YouTube fitness sped up his learning but killed his contentment, making him jealous and frustrated with his rate of progress
Living at home and eating whatever his mother cooked, he gained a lot of lean mass; once he chose his own food he ate Subway several times a day and entered a big surplus
Never being satisfied with your physique keeps you progressing; people who become fully content stop growing
Believing that getting stronger regardless of everything else would make him bigger, he combined powerlifting with a bulk and mostly got fat, gaining 70 lb quickly, mostly fat
His old program was so bad it left him stuck as a lifetime intermediate and injured over and over
Once you hit the point where extra calories no longer improve gym performance, a dirty bulk has stopped doing anything for you
Blaming the 'natural limit' is a way to reject personal responsibility and find an outside excuse for your own failures
Roughly 90% of people quit once they reach the intermediate stage; the 'limit' that kills them is mental
A common enhanced-influencer story is 'I did things right for about 5 years, stalled, then logically started PEDs'; he bought into it
Most PED 'harm reduction' content on YouTube is really promotion, and young men watch it to learn how to start
If you keep researching steroids 'out of curiosity', you are really preparing to take them; don't lie to yourself
Every young man who takes PEDs goes through a period of romanticising them, and that is what makes an illogical decision feel reasonable
In 2016-17, six years in, he was about 180 lb lean and 230-240 lb when fat, with good arms but no back, no lats, no width and many neglected weak points
Most young men who start PEDs are 4-5 years in with poor knowledge, poor programming and poor technique, not advanced lifters 15 years in
What you need is to stick with it, learn and keep grinding; PEDs hide laziness, ignorance and a fragile ego
As an immigrant without a green card he risked a felony and deportation by ordering PEDs, and still thought the reward was worth it
What saved him was that he could not source PEDs alone and had to go through a group of enhanced bodybuilders at his university gym
The enhanced lifters at his gym trained badly, mostly machines and cables for very high reps with bad form and light weights he could also move, yet they were twice his size
Taking PEDs can stop you from learning to train well, because the drugs cover up bad training
The trenbolone user he spent the most time with was aggressive, emotionally unstable, struggled to bench three plates and had a poor physique even on drugs
The bravado of the enhanced lifters he knew was a front for deep insecurity and unhappiness; the drugs were a cry for help
One lifter got huge in 2-3 weeks on an oral-only Dianabol cycle, then lost everything when he came off a few months later, could no longer enjoy natural training, and quit
Once you have trained enhanced, natural lifting can lose all its appeal, so you either go back on or stop lifting
The gym can give you confidence to use elsewhere, but it does not solve your life problems, and drug-built muscle you can lose overnight solves even less
Three of the nine enhanced lifters at that gym, in their 20s and 30s with no known conditions, died between 2016 and 2019, and nobody heard about it
PED users rarely die on stage; they die at home or in hospital, and social media only ever shows the upside
Years later, the one who stayed natural is bigger and stronger than all of them, because natural training lets you stay consistent and fits a long, healthy life
He feels pity, not hatred, toward PED users; those men saved his life and are part of why the channel exists
Unfollow influencers who push you toward PEDs; even if a natural preacher is secretly lying, listening to him still keeps you natural
Being healthy and fit into your 50s-70s is better than being massive for 2-3 years in your 20s
